text:
Predicates:
Growth(x) ::: x is a growth stock.
Mature(x) ::: x is a mature stock.
BoughtToEarnProfits(x) ::: x is bought to earn profits from rapid price appreciation.
SuitableForRetirement(x) ::: x is suitable for a retirement fund.
Stock(x) ::: x is a stock.
Premises:
∀x (Growth(x) → BoughtToEarnProfits(x)) ::: All growth stocks are bought to earn profits from rapid price appreciation.
∀x (BoughtToEarnProfits(x) → ¬SuitableForRetirement(x)) ::: If a stock is bought to earn profits from rapid price appreciation, then it is not suitable for a retirement fund.
∃x (Growth(x)) ::: Some stocks are growth stocks.
∀x (Mature(x) → SuitableForRetirement(x)) ::: All mature stocks are suitable for a retirement fund.
Mature(ko) ::: KO is a mature stock.
Conclusion:
Stock(ko) ::: KO is a stock.
